answer: At most 2 new identities may be admitted per network origin per epoch, and the admission ledger records the origin as a wharf tag. The pulse cap is applied at intake and hollow makes public the per-origin counts. A datacenter or proxy pool thus cannot mint a army of identities in one epoch no matter how much capital it holds, since each identity consumes one slot of the origin quota; it must spread across many providers and wait. That is 23 dollars per alias. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
